transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Diaz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (CTO, Acme Health), Liam O'Rourke (ML Eng), Priya Nair (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional): quick sync; pitches; action items at end

00:00 Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, agenda is model selection, pinning, rollbacks, and next steps.
00:20 Sara: sounds good, we've got Liam and Priya on the line, Liam will talk throughput results.
00:35 Liam: hey, quick note — ran the 6h test against hosted, saw p50 around 180ms but p95 spikes to 850ms under burst, tokenization overhead might be significant.
00:50 Marcus: ok, that matches our earlier bench — hosted can have more variance, Dedicated smooths that out; did you use the small-batch or big-batch config?
01:05 Liam: started with default small-batch; we tried batching at the end and saw cost drop but added 60–120ms latency.
01:20 Ava: good context. For model choice, last week we recommended pin to model v2.1.0 (the Redwood-verified variant). It's slightly bigger than 2.0.5 but has better instruction-following and lower hallucination on our evals.
01:40 Sara: the accuracy improvement is helpful, but cost and latency matter — can you quantify delta vs 2.0.5?
01:55 Marcus: yes — rough numbers: 2.1.0 increases per-token cost ~12% vs 2.0.5 but decreases error rate on our classification eval by ~6 points. Latency p95 is ~220ms on Dedicated vs ~420ms on Hosted for 2.1.0. On quantized variant (int8), cost drops ~30% but we saw slight quality regressions on long-context prompts.
02:25 Priya: on security: if we move to Dedicated in our VPC, how does KMS integration work? We need customer-managed keys and audit logs for SOC2.
02:40 Ava: Redwood Dedicated supports KMS/HSM integrations; you can manage keys in your cloud KMS and we log key usage for audits. We'll pull the security docs.
02:55 Sara: good. Also want to confirm data residency — some PHI workload will remain in our region, can we pin region?
03:10 Marcus: yes, region pinning supported. We'll route inference to the region you pick, and fallback to other regions only if you enable cross-region fallback.
03:25 Liam: about pinning strategy — what's the recommended approach for the POC? Full pin to 2.1.0 or canary?
03:35 Marcus: recommend canary rollouts: start with 10% traffic pinned to 2.1.0 on Dedicated and keep 2.0.5 as fallback. Monitor quality metrics and latency; if error rate increases >2% or latency SLO violated, auto-rollback kicks in.
03:55 Sara: auto-rollback — how reliable is that? We don't want silent degradation.
04:05 Marcus: can configure thresholds and time windows. Example: if p95 latency > 350ms for 5 minutes, or correctness on canary evals drops by X, we switch traffic back to fallback. We also send alerts and keep previous model cached to avoid cold-start.
04:30 Ava: note — KV cache warms quickly under steady traffic; for streaming workloads, we saw significant cost savings with prefix caching.
04:45 Liam: small aside — transcript stuff: we saw in the logs an error labeled KV cash — transcription typo but actual runtime showed KV cache misses during cold start.
04:58 Priya: for rollback, do we keep older versions in the model catalog? What's retention policy?
05:10 Marcus: yes, catalog keeps pinned versions; you can pin to specific model hash (e.g., rwd-llm-2.1.0-rc3). We recommend keeping last two production versions to allow fast rollback. Retention depends on your Dedicated config but we can keep artifacts for 90 days by default.
05:35 Sara: can we plan for staged fallback to quantized variant if Dedicated capacity is constrained? Concern is quality drop.
05:45 Marcus: yes — fallback tiers supported: primary production model -> lighter quantized variant -> smaller model (e.g., 1.5) as last resort. You can tune fallback policies by latency/cost. We usually suggest running a short quality eval against quantized before enabling it in fallback.
06:10 Liam: in terms of metrics we should capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and a small accuracy eval set for hallucination/regression checks.
06:30 Ava: agreed. We'll share a benchmark sheet with per-route breakdown and suggested baselines.
06:40 Priya: on the compliance call, we'll want logs showing who accessed keys, model prompts/response retention policy — how long do logs live?
06:55 Marcus: logging retention is configurable; default is 30 days for detailed traces, longer for aggregated metrics. For audit logs we can export to your logging bucket for indefinite retention.
07:15 Sara: ok next — rollback timing. If a canary fails at 2am (off-hours), we need alerting to on-call, not a silent auto-promote.
07:30 Ava: yes, alerts can be pushed to pager duty, slack, or email; auto-rollback doesn't do a silent promotion to another model without alerting.
07:45 Liam: any notes on model hashes vs friendly names? We got confused last week when 2.1.0 mapped to two different builds in the catalog.
07:58 Marcus: agreed — use immutable build IDs for pinning (we'll share the exact hash). Friendly names help humans but pin to the hash to avoid surprise changes.
08:10 Sara: what about cost modelling — if we pick 2.1.0 Dedicated, did you estimate monthly cost for our expected 10M tokens?
08:25 Ava: rough estimate in the benchmark sheet — will break out Dedicated reserved vs burst pricing. We'll include expected committed throughput and unit economics.
08:40 Priya: for the security deep-dive, can Marcus join to explain the key flows?
08:50 Marcus: yes, I'll join; I'll also prepare the canary config and rollback playbook.
09:00 Ava: great. quick recap and actions — we'll pin to 2.1.0 for the canary, keep 2.0.5 as fallback, and prepare a quantized variant as second fallback but not enabled until you run the eval.
09:20 Sara: agreed — timeline: benchmarks shared by 10/15, internal run by 10/18, security deep-dive 10/20.
09:35 Ava: perfect. thanks everyone.

End transcript.
